issues.failure_explanation: The proof verifies four tube-level identities, including (va ⋆M y)^+ = va ⋆M y with + the entrywise tube pseudoinverse, and then asserts that 'the same four equations' hold for the representation matrices R_va, R_y with ⋆M replaced by matrix product, concluding that R_y is the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of R_va. The first two identities transfer (the map x ↦ R_x is an algebra homomorphism), but the last two would have to become the transpose conditions (R_aR_y)^T = R_aR_y, which would require that tube conjugation correspond to matrix transposition, i.e. R_{x^*} = R_x^T. That property is exactly the Hilbert-algebra adjoint identity, which the paper itself states does not hold for a general M ('however it is easy to build counter examples for which this does not hold'), and it is not established under this lemma's hypotheses (only the row reality structure is assumed). Concretely, take any admissible all-real M, e.g. M = [[1,2],[3,-4]], and an idempotent a with Ma a 0/1 vector: R_{a⋆a^{winv}} = R_a is an idempotent projector that is not symmetric, so R_y is not the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of R_a, and the tube-level identity (a⋆y)^+ = a⋆y also fails for the entrywise + reading (M^{-1} of a 0/1 vector need not have ±1/0 entries). The uniqueness step of the proof therefore collapses.

failure_location.quote: The same four equation hold if we replace $\va$ with $\matR_\va$, $\vy$ with $\matR_\vy$ and $\Mprod$ with matrix product. Thus, $\matR_\vy$ is the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\matR_\va$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the Moore–Penrose transfer step and prove realness directly: since x is real, Mx has real entries at real rows and conjugate pairs at paired rows; entrywise inversion preserves this structure, so (Mx)^+ has it too, and by the column-structure of M^{-1} (Lemma lem:struct-Minv) the vector M^{-1}(Mx)^+ = x^{winv} is real. The explicit construction of y and the four-identity verification become unnecessary.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma lem:winv-realness does not establish its conclusion (realness of x^{winv}) as written. The conclusion itself is true and has a short direct proof (entrywise inversion preserves the real/conjugate-pair entry structure of Mx, and M^{-1} of such a vector is real by the mechanism of Lemma lem:struct-Minv), so Lemma lem:added-2 and all downstream uses of the weak inverse remain valid; no labelled result is invalidated.
issues.title: Invalid transfer of the four tube identities to the matrix Moore–Penrose axioms in the proof of Lemma lem:winv-realness
issues.why_classification: The lemma's statement is true and is re-established by a short, local argument already present in the paper (the conjugate-pair structure argument used for Lemmas lem:added-1/lem:added-13/lem:added-14); no new lemma or architecture is needed and every dependent use survives, so the defect is minor.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof justifies ||σ_1||_F ≥ ||σ_2||_F ≥ ⋯ by the unrestricted claim that a ≥M b implies ||â||_F ≥ ||b̂||_F for any two tubes. The hypothesis a ≥M b only says M(a−b) is real and entrywise non-negative, i.e. â − b̂ ≥ 0 entrywise; it does not order the squared entries when some entries of b̂ are negative. Counterexample inside the paper's own framework: M = I (rows real, invertible, a valid tubal ring), a = 0 and b the tube with Mb = (−1,0,…,0); then a ≥M b holds, but ||â||_F = 0 < 1 = ||b̂||_F. The conclusion of the corollary is still true for the singular tubes, because their transforms are entrywise non-negative (they are per-slice singular values, ordered non-increasingly as in Theorem thm:added-4), so the ordering of squares does follow; only the stated general justification is false.

issues.title: False general implication used to order the singular tubes in Corollary cor:added-1
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence local fix (adding the non-negativity of the transformed singular tubes, already available in the source) restores the proof; every substantive claim of the corollary and all downstream guarantees survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts the exact identity ||A − A_r||²_F = |c|^{-1}·Σ_j Σ_{i>r_j} hatσ²_{ij}. By the paper's own norm identity (Lemma lem:added-4: ||X̂||_F = |c|·||X||_F for M = cW), ||A − A_r||²_F = |c|^{-2}·||Â − Â_r||²_F, and ||Â − Â_r||²_F = Σ_j Σ_{i>r_j} hatσ²_{ij} because each transformed frontal slice of A_r is the r_j-truncated SVD of Â_j. Hence the correct factor is |c|^{-2}, not |c|^{-1}: for |c| ≠ 1 the displayed identity is false. For instance, with m = p = 1, n = 1 and M = [c], the error of the zero multirank truncation of a tube a is ||a||²_F while the stated formula gives |c|^{-1}·|ca|² = |c|·||a||²_F.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |c|^{-1} with |c|^{-2} in the displayed identity; the proof sketched ('essentially the same as the proof of the previous theorem'), executed slice-wise in the transform domain and combined with ||X̂||_F = |c|·||X||_F from Lemma lem:added-4, then yields the corrected identity exactly.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative error guarantee in Theorem thm:second-eckart-young is wrong whenever |c| ≠ 1; the optimality claim (A_r is the optimal ⋆M-multirank-r approximation) is unaffected, and no labelled downstream result uses the constant. The analogous formula in Theorem thm:first-eckart-young, expressed in primal tubes, is correct.
issues.title: Wrong scaling factor in the error formula of Theorem thm:second-eckart-young
issues.why_classification: A single-token correction to the stated constant makes the theorem true; the optimality statement, the regime (M = cW), and the proof strategy all survive, so no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.
